mainTopic: The sources and limits of יד (handle) and שומר (covering) for food טומאה: their פסוקים, הכשר, and minimum sizes
overview: Background: a יד is a handle-like part of food, such as a stalk, and a שומר is a protective covering, such as a shell or peel. The גמרא first asks where we learn that a יד brings טומאה into food. It settles on the פסוק about food (ויקרא 11:38), and explains that the extra פסוק about the שומר of a נבלה teaches its own topic, even though a קל וחומר could teach it. When a פסוק can teach something new, though, we read it that way. רב חביבא offers another answer: the שומר of a נבלה acts like a handle, so its extra teaching goes to the law of יד. Next, רב יהודה בר ישמעאל challenges learning שומר from 'on any sowing seed', using a pomegranate and parts of meat that are never sown. The גמרא answers that three 'sowing' words cover seeds, trees, and meat, eggs and fish. Then רב and רבי יוחנן argue whether a handle also counts for הכשר, and the גמרא explains their argument from a פסוק or from logic; a ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן. Finally they argue whether a handle or covering counts for food smaller than a כזית or a כפול. A ברייתא about two bones with half-olives of flesh challenges both views, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why give the extra verse to the handle and not to coverings in general?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier idea: the extra פסוק about the שומר of a נבלה should be used for the laws of שומר in general, not for יד. That would leave no source that a יד brings in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: if the verse is not needed for the covering of a carcass, use it for coverings in general. A covering brings in impurity, and a covering joins together to make the size. But we would still have no source that a handle brings in impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the earlier move that used the extra נבלה פסוק to teach that a יד brings in טומאה. It says that the extra פסוק could just as easily go to the general laws of שומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the rule of אם אינו ענין, an extra פסוק gets 'moved' to a nearby topic. The challenge is that the closest topic is שומר in food, where two laws need sources: that a שומר brings in טומאה and that it joins to make the size. If the extra פסוק goes there, nothing is left to teach that a יד brings in טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for its own topic, apply it to another topic. This is a rule for using a 'spare' פסוק.
A protective covering of food, such as a shell or peel.
A handle of food, such as a stalk or stem.
To bring in, meaning to pass טומאה into the food.
To join together with the food to make up the minimum size.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two parts. A שומר is a covering that protects the food, and a יד is a handle you hold it by. They follow different rules.

phrases.english: But say: if it is not needed for the matter
of the covering of a carcass,
apply it to the matter of coverings in general,
a covering brings in, and a covering joins together,
but a handle bringing in, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לְשׁוֹמֵר דִּנְבֵלָה, תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לְשׁוֹמֵר דְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the derivation from the earlier part of the sugya, which used the extra נבלה פסוק to teach that a יד brings in טומאה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the spare נבלה פסוק teaches that a יד brings in טומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A spare פסוק should go to the closest related topic, which is שומר in general. That leaves the law of יד with no source.

steps.title: Back to the original source: the handle verse is about bringing in
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the נבלה-based derivation and returns to its first source. The פסוק about food that teaches יד is written in the setting of bringing in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, from the very start, where the handle is written, it is written about bringing in impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by going back to its original source for יד, the פסוק about food. It points out that this פסוק is about food receiving טומאה, so it directly teaches that a יד brings in טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, someone worried that the food פסוק only taught that a יד passes טומאה out. Now the גמרא notes that the פסוק describes food becoming טמא, which is bringing in. So the law of יד bringing in comes straight from that פסוק, and the extra נבלה פסוק is no longer needed for it.

keyTerms.meaning: From the outset, from the start.
Bringing in, meaning receiving טומאה.
Rather. Here it signals dropping one approach and going back to another.

phrases.english: Rather, from the outset,
when the handle is written,
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק about food, ויקרא 11:38, 'טמא הוא לכם'.

phrases.english: it is written about bringing in.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מֵעִיקָּרָא כִּי כְּתִיבָא יָד, אַהַכְנָסָה כְּתִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by going back to the first source instead of the spare נבלה פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Return to the original source with a new reading of its setting
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We needed the spare נבלה פסוק to teach that a יד brings in טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The food פסוק itself is about bringing in, so it teaches that a יד brings in טומאה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This frees up the נבלה פסוק, which sets up the next question about what that פסוק is for.

steps.title: Then why do we need the verse about a carcass's covering?
steps.stepSummary: Now that the law of יד is learned from the food פסוק, the גמרא asks what the פסוק about the שומר of a נבלה teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, why do I need the verse about the covering of a carcass?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what purpose the נבלה פסוק now serves, since it is no longer being used to teach the law of יד. This question sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every פסוק must teach something. Once the earlier use is taken away, the נבלה פסוק looks extra again, so the גמרא needs to find its job.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? This asks what a source is for.
An animal that died without proper שחיטה. It is a source of טומאה.

phrases.english: But then, the covering of a carcass,
why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שׁוֹמֵר דִּנְבֵלָה, לְמָה לִי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A result of step 2: the נבלה פסוק is now left without a job.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the פסוק about the שומר of a נבלה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the law of יד comes from the food פסוק, the נבלה פסוק seems to teach nothing.

steps.title: The carcass verse teaches its own topic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the נבלה פסוק teaches about itself: the laws of שומר also apply to the טומאה of a נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is needed for its own topic. It teaches that a שומר matters for the טומאה of a נבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא treated this פסוק as spare and moved it to another topic. Now it is used in its plain meaning, for a נבלה itself.

keyTerms.meaning: For itself, meaning the פסוק teaches its own plain topic.

phrases.english: For itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְגוּפֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Using the פסוק for its plain topic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The נבלה פסוק is spare and teaches nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that the laws of שומר apply to the טומאה of a נבלה.

steps.title: But what exactly would it teach about a carcass?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא presses the answer. If the פסוק teaches joining together, the משנה says a שומר of a נבלה does not join. If it teaches bringing in and passing out, that is already known by a קל וחומר from יד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for what law? If to join together, you said it does not join! If to bring in and pass out, that comes from a קל וחומר from the handle!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer 'for itself' by asking which law the פסוק teaches. Each possible law is either contradicted by the משנה or already known by a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Joining together cannot be the law, because the משנה rules that a שומר of a נבלה does not join to make the size. Bringing in and passing out are also not new: if even a weaker part like a יד brings in and passes out טומאה, a שומר surely does. So the פסוק still seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger case: if this is true of the weaker case, it is surely true of the stronger one.
To pass out, meaning to pass טומאה from the food to something else.
And for what? This asks which law the source teaches.

phrases.english: And for what?
If to join together,
you said it does not join!
phrases.notes: 'You said' points back to our משנה, which rules that a שומר of a נבלה does not join.

phrases.english: If to bring in and pass out,
it comes by a קל וחומר from a handle!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאי? אִי לְאִצְטְרוֹפֵי – אָמְרַתְּ לָא מִצְטָרֵף!
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer 'for itself' from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the נבלה פסוק teaches its own topic.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both possible laws fail. Joining together goes against the משנה, and bringing in and passing out are already known by a קל וחומר from יד.
steps.confusionAlert: The קל וחומר works because a יד is weaker than a שומר: a יד does not join to make the size, but a שומר does. So whatever a יד does, a שומר surely does too.

steps.title: The תורה sometimes writes out what a קל וחומר could teach
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that sometimes the תורה takes the trouble to write out a law even though a קל וחומר could teach it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Something that could come by a קל וחומר, the verse took the trouble and wrote it anyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last challenge with a general rule. A פסוק may state a law outright even if a קל וחומר could already teach it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that a פסוק cannot be 'wasted' on something logic already teaches. The answer rejects that assumption. So the נבלה פסוק teaches that a שומר brings in and passes out טומאה, even though a קל וחומר from יד could have taught it too.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק took the trouble and wrote it, meaning the תורה wrote it out anyway.
A matter, a thing.

steps.whatToRemember: A יד brings in טומאה, learned from the food פסוק (ויקרא 11:38). The נבלה פסוק teaches its own topic, and it is not a problem that a קל וחומר could also teach this, because sometimes the תורה writes out what a קל וחומר could teach.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general principle that comes up across ש״ס: a פסוק can state a law outright even when a קל וחומר could already teach it.

phrases.english: A matter that could come by a קל וחומר,
the verse took the trouble and wrote it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִילְּתָא דְּאָתְיָא בְּקַל וְחוֹמֶר – טָרַח וְכָתַב לַהּ קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: General rule that the תורה may write out something a קל וחומר could teach
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A פסוק is not used for a law that a קל וחומר already teaches.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה sometimes writes out a law anyway, so the נבלה פסוק can teach that a שומר brings in and passes out טומאה.

steps.title: Then say the food פסוק also only teaches bringing in
steps.stepSummary: If the תורה sometimes writes out what a קל וחומר could teach, then the food פסוק could also be teaching only 'bringing in', not joining.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then about a regular שומר (of food), I can tell you that the פסוק teaches that it brings in טומאה. Something that could be learned by a קל וחומר, the פסוק took the trouble to write anyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the answer from Step 6 to attack the food פסוק. If a פסוק can repeat what a קל וחומר already teaches, maybe the food פסוק does not teach joining at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the food פסוק was read as teaching joining, because bringing in and passing out were already known by a קל וחומר from יד. Step 6 said the תורה sometimes writes things anyway. If so, the food פסוק could simply be teaching bringing in, and then there is no source that a שומר joins.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if what you just said is true)
A regular שומר, meaning the shell or peel of ordinary food
To bring in טומאה to the food
The פסוק took the trouble and wrote it out

phrases.english: If so,
regarding a shell in general,
I can say to you: it teaches that it brings in impurity,
and a matter that could come from a kal vachomer —
the verse took the trouble and wrote it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, שׁוֹמֵר דְּעָלְמָא, אֵימָא לָךְ: לְהַכְנִיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of Step 6 against the food-פסוק derivation
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the food פסוק teaches צירוף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a פסוק may repeat a קל וחומר, the food פסוק could be teaching only להכניס, which leaves no source for צירוף.

steps.title: When a פסוק can teach something new, we read it that way
steps.stepSummary: Where a פסוק can be read as teaching something new, we read it that way. We only say 'the תורה wrote out a קל וחומר' when there is no other choice.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where there is something to learn from it, we learn it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a פסוק is read as teaching something new whenever that is possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For food, the פסוק can teach joining, so we read it that way. For a נבלה, the משנה says its שומר does not join, so nothing new is left to teach. Only there do we say the תורה wrote out what a קל וחומר already teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: To learn a new teaching from a פסוק
We learn it out (we read it as teaching something)

steps.whatToRemember: 'טרח וכתב קרא' is a last resort. If a פסוק can teach something new, we read it as teaching something new.

phrases.english: Where there is something to expound,
we expound it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא לְמִידְרַשׁ, דָּרְשִׁינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rule of interpretation: prefer a new teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The food פסוק might be repeating what the קל וחומר already teaches.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the food פסוק can teach צירוף, it teaches צירוף. The נבלה פסוק, which cannot, is a case of טרח וכתב.

steps.title: רב חביבא: the שומר of a נבלה works like a handle
steps.stepSummary: רב חביבא goes back to the idea of learning יד from the נבלה פסוק. A נבלה's שומר only brings in and passes out טומאה, which is exactly what a handle does. So its lesson is applied to handles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חביבא said: the שומר of a נבלה is different. Since it does the job of a handle, we apply it to the law of a handle.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חביבא returns to the earlier proposal of learning the law of יד from the נבלה פסוק. He answers the old question of why it should not be applied to שומר in general instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומר of food also joins, but a שומר of a נבלה does not join. It only brings in and passes out טומאה, just like a handle. So if the נבלה פסוק is free to teach something else, it belongs with handles, not with שומרים.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
An animal that died without proper שחיטה
The job of a handle: bringing in and passing out טומאה without joining
We apply it (literally, we throw it onto)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a continuation of Step 8. רב חביבא is going back to the earlier idea of learning יד from the נבלה פסוק, which the גמרא had dropped in Step 2.

phrases.english: Rav Chaviva said:
The protective part of a carcass is different,
since it does the job of a handle,
we apply it to the law of a handle.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חֲבִיבָא אָמַר: שָׁאנֵי שׁוֹמֵר דִּנְבֵלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the food-פסוק discussion and gives a new answer to the challenge of step 1. That revives the earlier נבלה-based derivation of יד.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: a נבלה's שומר functions like a יד
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A free נבלה פסוק should be applied to שומר in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because a נבלה's שומר only brings in and passes out, like a handle, its extra teaching goes to יד.

steps.title: Challenge from the pomegranate's tip and flower
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בר ישמעאל begins a challenge from a משנה. The tip of a pomegranate joins with the fruit, but its flower does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה בר ישמעאל challenged this from what we learned in a משנה: the tip of a pomegranate joins, but its flower does not join.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge by quoting a משנה. The actual question built on this משנה comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The target is the teaching that a שומר of food joins with the food to make up the needed size. The משנה gives two parts of a pomegranate with different rules. The tip joins, but the flower does not.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it (raised a strong objection)
The crown-like tip sticking out at the top of a pomegranate
The flower (blossom) at the tip
Joins with the food to make up the needed size for טומאה

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר יִשְׁמָעֵאל,
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda bar Yishmael challenged this:
What about that which we learned in a mishna:
the protruding tip of a pomegranate joins together,
but its flower does not join together.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר יִשְׁמָעֵאל, הָא דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against the teaching that a שומר of food joins
steps.kashyaTarget: The teaching that a שומר of food joins with the food
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: a משנה gives different rules for two outer parts of a pomegranate. The full objection follows in the next lines.

steps.title: Why should the pomegranate's tip join if it is not planted that way?
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בר ישמעאל completes his challenge: the פסוק speaks of seed as it is sown, but a pomegranate is not planted with its tip, so why does the tip join?
steps.simpleTranslation: And why should it join? Read here: 'on any sowing seed', and that is not the case here!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge it began in step 10. If the source for שומר is 'on any sowing seed', the tip of a pomegranate should not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'sowing' suggests that only parts that stay with the seed when it is planted count as its שומר. Pomegranates are not planted together with their tips, yet the משנה says the tip joins. So the source seems too narrow to explain the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: And why? An opening that signals a challenge.
Sowing seed, meaning seed in the form in which it is planted.
And it is not there, meaning this case does not fit.

phrases.english: And why? Read here:
'on any sowing seed', and that is not the case here!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:37. A pomegranate is not planted with its tip, so the tip is not part of the 'sowing seed'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? קְרִי כָּאן ״עַל כׇּל זֶרַע זֵרוּעַ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from the pomegranate משנה that step 10 began.
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning שומר from the words 'on any sowing seed'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק points to the seed as it is planted. The pomegranate's tip is not planted, yet the משנה says it joins.

steps.title: A second challenge from the parts of meat that join
steps.stepSummary: A further problem: the משנה says hide, gravy and spices join with meat for טומאת אוכלין, but meat is never sown. Where does that come from?
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, what we learned in the משנה: the hide, the gravy, the spices, and so on, join to make it טמא with food-טומאה. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger challenge. Meat is not planted at all, so a 'sowing' פסוק should not cover it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pomegranate is at least a plant. Meat, with its hide and gravy, has nothing to do with planting. If the only source is 'on any sowing seed', the rule in this משנה has no source.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, which brings a second challenge.
Hide, congealed gravy, and spices that are attached to meat.
Joins together to make up the needed amount.
The טומאה that food carries.
From where do we know this? A request for a source.

phrases.english: And furthermore, what we learned in the משנה:
The hide, the gravy, the spices, and so on.
join to make it טמא with food-טומאה. From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, הָא דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to the same source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שומר is learned from 'on any sowing seed'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Meat is never sown, yet its protective parts join. A 'sowing' source cannot explain that.

steps.title: Three sowing words cover seeds, trees, and meat, eggs and fish
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק has three 'sowing' words. One teaches שומר for seeds, one for trees, and one for meat, eggs and fish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, three words are written: 'on any seed', 'sowing', 'that is sown'. One is for the שומר of seeds, one is for the שומר of trees, and the other is for the שומר of meat, eggs and fish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers both challenges. Each extra word in the פסוק adds another kind of food to the rule of שומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said 'seed' only once. Since it repeats the 'sowing' idea three times, the extra words widen the rule. Trees cover the pomegranate tip, and the third word covers meat, eggs and fish, even though none of these are sown.

keyTerms.meaning: Three words or phrases in the פסוק.
Seeds or grains.
Trees, meaning fruit from trees.
The other one.

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of שומר is not limited to things that are planted. Three 'sowing' words in ויקרא 11:37 extend it to seeds, tree fruit, and meat, eggs and fish.

phrases.english: Rather, three words are written:
'on any seed', 'sowing', 'that is sown'.
One is for the שומר of seeds,
and one is for the שומר of trees,
the other is for the שומר of meat, eggs and fish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא תְּלָתָא קְרָאֵי כְּתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both challenges from steps 11 and 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק: the repeated words widen the rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק was read as covering only seed in its planted form.
steps.terutzMaskana: The three 'sowing' words cover seeds, trees, and meat, eggs and fish.

steps.title: A handle counts for טומאה but not for הכשר
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that a handle passes טומאה into and out of food, but water touching only the handle does not make the food ready to become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: A handle counts for טומאה, but a handle does not count for הכשר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רב sets a limit on how far the idea of a handle (יד) reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא learned that a handle brings טומאה in and out of the food it is attached to. Food also needs to get wet (הכשר) before it can become טמא at all. רב says the handle does not help for this: wetting only the handle does not prepare the food itself.

keyTerms.meaning: A handle counts for passing טומאה into and out of food.
Making food ready to become טמא by having liquid touch it.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that a handle counts for everything. It passes טומאה, but liquid that touches only the handle does not do the הכשר of the food.
steps.whyThisMatters: This divides the laws of food טומאה into two stages. Getting ready to become טמא (הכשר) and actually receiving טומאה follow different rules.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי, אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: רב חייא בר אשי said that רב said:
A handle counts for טומאה,
but a handle does not count for הכשר.
phrases.notes: Food must get wet before it can become טמא. רב says wetting only the handle is not enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי, אָמַר רַב: יֵשׁ יָד לְטוּמְאָה, וְאֵין יָד לְהֶכְשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where שומר comes from to a new limit on the power of a handle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A handle passes טומאה into and out of food, but liquid on the handle does not do the הכשר of the food.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says a handle counts for both טומאה and הכשר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees with רב and holds that a handle counts both for טומאה and for making food ready to become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: A handle counts for טומאה and also for הכשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן's opinion, which argues with what רב just said in step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said a handle counts for טומאה but not for הכשר. רבי יוחנן says it counts for both. So if water touches only the handle, the food attached to it is now ready to become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: A handle, such as a stem or stalk attached to food
Making food ready to become טמא, which happens when it gets wet
Ritual impurity

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two jobs separate. Passing טומאה is one thing. Making the food ready to receive טומאה (הכשר) is a different thing. רב and רבי יוחנן agree on the first and argue only about the second.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
A handle counts for impurity and for making food susceptible.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רב's ruling in step 14
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A handle counts both for passing טומאה and for הכשר

steps.title: What is the root of the argument between רב and רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב and רבי יוחנן are really arguing about and says it can be explained by logic or by a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are they arguing about? You can say it is a matter of logic, or you can say it is a matter of a פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the deeper reason behind the argument. It is setting up the next move by offering two possible roots: logic or a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is not asking who is right. It wants to know what each side is based on. It lists two options, and the next step explains the פסוק option first.

keyTerms.meaning: What are they arguing about? The root of the argument
If you want, say... It introduces one possible explanation
Logic, reasoning
A פסוק

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?
If you want, say it is about logic,
if you want, say it is about a verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the root of the argument between steps 14 and 15
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the underlying basis of the argument between רב and רבי יוחנן about a handle and הכשר?

steps.title: The פסוק explanation: how far back does a teaching word reach?
steps.stepSummary: רב holds that a teaching word in a פסוק connects only to the phrase right before it. רבי יוחנן holds that it also connects to the phrase before that one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is about a פסוק. One master (רב) holds that a פסוק is explained with the phrase right before it, but not with the phrase before that. The other master (רבי יוחנן) holds that a פסוק is explained with the phrase right before it, and also with the phrase before that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the פסוק-based root of the argument. Both sides agree on the same word in the פסוק, but they disagree about how far back in the פסוק that word reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first speaks about water being put on the food, which is הכשר. Next it says the food becomes טמא, and then comes the word that teaches us about a handle. רב says that word connects only to the nearest phrase, טומאה, so a handle counts only for טומאה. רבי יוחנן says it also reaches back to the water phrase, so a handle counts for הכשר too.

keyTerms.meaning: One master holds. Here it means one of the two sides, רב or רבי יוחנן
A word in a פסוק is explained together with the phrase right before it
The phrase before the one right before it, two steps back

steps.whatToRemember: רב and רבי יוחנן argue about a reading rule. Does a teaching word connect only to the phrase right before it (רב), or also to the phrase before that one (רבי יוחנן)? This decides whether a handle counts for הכשר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reading rule is a general tool for explaining פסוקים, so it can come up in other places too, not just with handles.

phrases.english: If you want, say it is about a verse:
phrases.notes: The פסוק is ויקרא 11:38. The word לכם, "for you," is the word that teaches us about a handle.

phrases.english: One master holds: a verse is explained with what is right before it,
phrases.notes: This is רב. The phrase right before לכם is "it is טמא."

phrases.english: and not with what comes before that.
phrases.notes: The earlier phrase is "if water is put," which is about הכשר. So for רב, a handle does not count for הכשר.

phrases.english: And the other master holds: a verse is explained with what is right before it,
and also with what comes before that.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא קְרָא, מָר סָבַר: מִקְרָא נִדְרָשׁ לְפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 by explaining the פסוק option
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue whether a teaching word in a פסוק reaches only the phrase right before it (רב) or also the phrase before that one (רבי יוחנן).

steps.title: Second explanation: the argument is about logic
steps.stepSummary: The argument can also be explained by logic. רבי יוחנן holds that הכשר is the first stage of טומאה. רב holds that it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say they argue about logic. One sage holds that making food ready is the beginning of טומאה. The other holds that making food ready is not the beginning of טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second answer it promised in Step 16. The argument between רב and רבי יוחנן can also come from simple logic, not only from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If הכשר is just the first stage of טומאה, then whatever passes טומאה (like a handle) should also pass הכשר. That is רבי יוחנן's view. If הכשר is a separate thing, a handle can count for טומאה but not for הכשר. That is רב's view.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: introduces another possible answer
Logic, reasoning (as opposed to a פסוק)
Making food ready to become טמא, through contact with water or another liquid
The beginning stage of becoming טמא

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא just says 'one sage' (מר) twice without names. The first מר, who says הכשר is the beginning of טומאה, is רבי יוחנן. The second מר is רב.

phrases.english: If you want, say they argue about logic:

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: הֶכְשֵׁר תְּחִלַּת טוּמְאָה הוּא,
phrases.english: One sage holds: making food ready is the beginning of טומאה,
phrases.notes: This sage is רבי יוחנן, so a handle works for both.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: הֶכְשֵׁר לָאו תְּחִלַּת טוּמְאָה הוּא.
phrases.english: and the other sage holds: making food ready is not the beginning of טומאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא סְבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the logic-based answer, alongside the פסוק-based answer of Step 17, to the question of Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the basis of the argument between רב and רבי יוחנן?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue about whether הכשר is the first stage of טומאה. רבי יוחנן says yes, so the handle counts for הכשר. רב says no, so it does not.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a handle counts for הכשר just as it counts for טומאה. It also teaches that produce becomes ready to become טמא only once it is picked.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא is taught that matches רבי יוחנן: Just as a handle counts for טומאה, a handle also counts for making food ready. And just as produce only becomes טמא after it is picked, it also only becomes ready to become טמא once it is picked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רבי יוחנן said: a handle counts for הכשר too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the ברייתא directly matches רבי יוחנן against רב. The second half adds a parallel rule: produce still attached to the ground cannot become טמא. In the same way, it cannot be made ready while still attached. It becomes ready only once it is picked.

keyTerms.meaning: A handle, such as a stem, attached to food
Able to become טמא
They will be picked, detached from the ground

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא backs רבי יוחנן: a handle counts both for טומאה and for הכשר.

phrases.english: A ברייתא is taught that matches רבי יוחנן:
Just as a handle counts for טומאה,
so too a handle counts for making food ready,
and just as they cannot become טמא
except once they are picked,
so too they cannot be made ready
until they are picked.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא supporting the view of רבי יוחנן explained in Steps 15 and 18.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that a handle counts for הכשר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says 'just as there is a handle for טומאה, there is a handle for הכשר'.

steps.title: רב: no handle or shell for very small food
steps.stepSummary: רב says a handle does not count if the food is smaller than a כזית. A protective shell does not count if the food is smaller than a כפול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: A handle does not count for less than an olive-sized piece of food. A protective shell does not count for less than a bean-sized piece of food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new argument between רב and רבי יוחנן. Here רב says that a handle or shell attached to a tiny piece of food does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about size. In רב's view, a handle only counts when the food it holds is at least a כזית. A שומר (shell or peel) only counts when the food it covers is at least a כפול. Below those sizes, they are treated as unimportant.

keyTerms.meaning: The size of an olive
A protective covering, like a shell or peel
The size of a bean

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: אֵין יָד לְפָחוֹת מִכְּזַיִת,
phrases.english: רב said: A handle does not count for less than an olive-size,
phrases.notes: He means less than an olive-size of food attached to the handle.

phrases.english: and a protective covering does not count for less than a bean-size.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new argument between the same two sages, about minimum sizes for יד and שומר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A handle does not count for food smaller than a כזית. A שומר does not count for food smaller than a כפול.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: handle and shell count even for very small food
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees. A handle counts even for less than a כזית, and a protective shell counts even for less than a כפול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: A handle does count for less than an olive-sized piece of food, and a protective shell does count for less than a bean-sized piece of food.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the opposite view to רב: even small pieces of food have a handle and a shell that count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the size of the food does not decide whether its handle or shell counts. Even with a tiny piece of food, the handle and the shell still have their legal role. This is a direct mirror of רב's statement, word for word, with 'yes' in place of 'no'.

keyTerms.meaning: The handle does count
The protective covering does count
For less than (a certain size)

steps.whatToRemember: רב: a handle needs at least a כזית of food, and a shell needs at least a כפול. רבי יוחנן: no minimum size, both count even for smaller food.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: יֵשׁ יָד לְפָחוֹת מִכְּזַיִת,
phrases.english: And רבי יוחנן said: A handle does count for less than an olive-size,
and a protective covering does count for less than a bean-size.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוחנן's opposing view to רב's statement in Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A handle counts even for food smaller than a כזית. A שומר counts even for food smaller than a כפול.

steps.title: A ברייתא where two bones with half-olives of flesh make a house טמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. Two bones each carry half a כזית of flesh from a dead body, and only their bare ends are under a house's roof. The house becomes טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: Two bones have two half-olive pieces of flesh on them. Someone put the ends of both bones into a house, and the house covers those ends. The house is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge the opinions from steps 20 and 21. Here the bones act as handles that bring the flesh's טומאה into the house, even though each piece of flesh is only half a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the bare bone ends are inside the house, not the flesh. So the house can only be טמא if each bone works like a handle connecting it to the flesh, and the two half-pieces add up to a כזית. That seems to clash with רב, who said a handle does not count for less than a כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: Overlies or covers. Something that forms a roof over טומאת מת spreads the טומאה to what is under it (אֹהֶל).
Halves of olive-sized pieces. Each piece alone is too small to spread טומאת מת.
Bones. Here they serve as the 'handles' attached to the flesh.
Ritually impure.

steps.confusionAlert: The flesh itself is NOT inside the house. Only the bare ends of the bones are. The whole question is whether the bones carry the flesh's טומאה in, the way a handle does.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵּי עֲצָמוֹת, וַעֲלֵיהֶן שְׁנֵי חֲצָאֵי זֵיתִים,
phrases.english: Two bones, and on them two halves of olive-bulks [of flesh from a dead body],
and he brought the ends of both of them into a house,
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'two', the word in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, reads 'both'.

phrases.english: and the house overlies them (the bone ends) —
the house is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the argument between רב and רבי יוחנן in steps 20-21 about whether a handle counts for less than a כזית.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule (step 20) that a handle does not count when the food is smaller than a כזית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The house is טמא only through the bone ends. That means the bones act as handles for half-olive pieces, which is less than a כזית, and the pieces combine. This goes against רב.

steps.title: יהודה בן נקוסא asks how two bones can join to make a כזית
steps.stepSummary: Still inside the same ברייתא, יהודה בן נקוסא, quoting רבי יעקב, disagrees with the first opinion. He asks how two separate bones could combine to make a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהודה בן נקוסא says in the name of רבי יעקב: How can two bones join together to make a כזית?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second opinion that disagrees with the first. It doubts that the two half-olive pieces on two separate bones can count together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion let the two half-pieces combine through their bone handles. This opinion rejects that combination, which suggests handles do not work this way for small amounts. If so, it seems to clash with רבי יוחנן (step 21), who said a handle counts even for less than a כזית. So the ברייתא as a whole seems to cause trouble for both אמוראים.

keyTerms.meaning: Join together. Two smaller amounts are counted as one full measure.
An olive-bulk. The minimum amount of flesh from a dead body needed to spread טומאה through an אֹהֶל.
How? Here it is a challenge meaning 'how could this possibly be?'

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא has two sides. The first opinion lets half-olives combine through bone handles, which seems to go against רב. יהודה בן נקוסא rejects that, which seems to go against רבי יוחנן.

phrases.aramaic: יְהוּדָה בֶּן נָקוֹסָא אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Yehuda ben Nekosa says in the name of Rabbi Yaakov:
How can two bones join together to make an olive-bulk?

steps.triggerLanguage: יְהוּדָה בֶּן נָקוֹסָא אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quoted ברייתא from step 22 with a disagreeing opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule (step 21) that a handle counts even for less than a כזית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This opinion refuses to let half-olive pieces combine through bone handles. That suggests handles do not count for small amounts, which goes against רבי יוחנן.
